record.paper_title: Positive and free boundary solutions to singular nonlinear elliptic problems with absorption: an overview and open problems
record.original_question: For problem (III), what is the structure of the set of compact-support solutions when such solutions exist?

evidence.quote: it would be interesting to know if there is more than one positive solution in the first case k − α < 1 and if, also in this case, there are compact support solutions. Information on the structure of the set of compact support solutions is interesting as well.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $\Omega \subset \mathbb{R}^N$ ($N \geq 1$) be a bounded domain with smooth boundary. Fix real exponents $0 < k < 1$ and $0 < \alpha < 1$ and a real spectral parameter $\lambda > 0$. Consider the singular semilinear elliptic boundary-value problem
$$
\begin{cases}
-\Delta u + u^{-\alpha}\,\chi_{\{u>0\}} = \lambda\, u^{k} & \text{in } \Omega,\\
u \geq 0 & \text{in } \Omega,\\
u = 0 & \text{on } \partial\Omega,
\end{cases}
\tag{III}
$$
where the absorption term $u^{-\alpha}\chi_{\{u>0\}}$ is interpreted in the maximal monotone graph sense (so that $u^{-\alpha}\chi_{\{u>0\}} = 0$ wherever $u = 0$). A weak solution $u \in H_0^1(\Omega) \cap L^\infty(\Omega)$ is called a *compact-support solution* if its positivity set $\{x \in \Omega : u(x) > 0\}$ has its closure strictly contained in $\Omega$ (so that the free boundary $\partial\{u>0\} \cap \Omega$ is non-empty).

Assume one is in the parameter regime $k - \alpha < 1$ in which non-trivial non-negative solutions to (III) are known to exist for sufficiently large $\lambda$. Describe completely the structure of the set
$$
\mathcal{C}(\lambda) = \{u : u \text{ is a compact-support solution of (III) for the given } \lambda\}.
$$
In particular, determine: (i) for which values of $\lambda$ the set $\mathcal{C}(\lambda)$ is non-empty; (ii) whether $\mathcal{C}(\lambda)$ may contain more than one element (multiplicity); (iii) whether $\mathcal{C}(\lambda)$ admits a continuous parametrization (e.g., a continuum or branch in $\lambda$ bifurcating from the trivial solution or from infinity); and (iv) the geometric structure of the corresponding free boundaries.
artifact.category_tag: singular semilinear elliptic problems with absorption
artifact.status_search_result: The question is posed as an open problem in a 2014 survey on singular nonlinear elliptic problems with absorption. Subsequent works by Díaz, Hernández and collaborators (e.g., on indefinite sublinear elliptic problems and on spectral problems with strong absorption, 2015–2025) have addressed related existence and multiplicity issues, but no source found gives a complete description of the structure of the set of compact-support solutions in the regime $k-\alpha<1$. The problem appears to remain open.

status_evidence.title: Positive and Free Boundary Solutions to Singular Nonlinear Elliptic Problems with Absorption: An Overview and Open Problems
status_evidence.snippet: Surveys existence and multiplicity of positive and/or compact-support solutions to semilinear elliptic equations with singular absorption terms; lists open problems.
status_evidence.claim: The structural description of compact-support solutions for Problem (III) is presented as an open problem.

status_evidence.title: On the existence of positive solutions and solutions with compact support for a spectral nonlinear elliptic problem with strong absorption
status_evidence.snippet: Studies existence of positive solutions and of solutions with compact support for a spectral elliptic problem with a strong (non-Lipschitz) absorption term.
status_evidence.claim: Subsequent work treats existence questions but does not give a complete structural classification of the compact-support solution set.

status_evidence.title: Non-negative and positive solutions for some indefinite sublinear elliptic problems
status_evidence.snippet: Recent (2025) work by Díaz, Hernández and Ilyasov on indefinite sublinear problems showing existence of compact-support solutions under additional assumptions.
status_evidence.claim: Indicates ongoing research; full structure of compact-support solution set still being studied.
